text:
Alex W: seeing a burst of apiserver 429s in eu-west, controller-manager leader flapping twice in the last 3m. GPU node attaches are failing around the same time.
Maria S: yup saw alerts, rate of new pod creates that need GPUs spiked when an internal batch job kicked off.
Ryan (oncall): apiserver metrics show conntrack drops + SNAT port exhaustion on the NATGW -> 429s and short-lived watch reconnects.
sre-bot: Incident detected: apiserver_429_rate > 5% for 2m in eu-west1. Paging oncall.
Jin (infra): NATGW metrics confirm ephemeral port exhaustion, outbound port usage near 64k limit per NAT. We have many parallel kubelet/attach flows hitting external control plane and storage APIs.
Alex W: controller-manager losing leader leases when apiserver 429s happen. That causes scheduling churn and triggers kubelet to reprovision in some GPU pools. Onboard attach storms make the NAT worse -> feedback loop.
Maria S: can we throttle node onboarding/attach from the provisioner side? The autoscaler is respecting targets but it's too eager during that batch job.
Ryan (oncall): temp mitigation: reduce autoscaler scale-up bursts to 2 nodes and pause new batch jobs. I can apply a cluster-autoscaler flag.
Jin (infra): longer term we need either increase NAT capacity (additional NATGW / EIP pools) or move control-plane traffic to internal endpoints for attach/storage APIs. Increasing NAT has cost impact though.
Alex W: also saw lots of short-lived watch reconnections causing apiserver CPU spike. Could we enable client-side backoff on controllers to reduce watch fanout? Controller-manager tuning could help.
Maria S: checklist: 1) pause batch job (in progress), 2) set CA max-bulk-scale to 2 (Ryan doing), 3) add temporary extra NATGW (Jin?), 4) apply leader election graceful window to controller-manager to tolerate short blips.
Ryan (oncall): paused batch job. Applying CA flag now: `--scale-up-delay=30s --max-node-provision-time=15m`
Jin (infra): provisioning extra NATGW now, ETA ~6m. Will route a subset of egress through new gateway to spread ports. Cost estimate: +$0.8/hr for eu-west temporary.
Alex W: thanks. Can we also add a short-lived prefix/KV cache bypass to reduce apiserver read pressure? Might reduce watch reconnections.
Maria S: happy to add caching rule on read-heavy controllers for 30m window.
Ryan (oncall): after CA change and pausing workload, apiserver 429s dropped to ~0.8%. controller-manager leader stable for last 3m.
Jin (infra): NATGW provisioned and routes in place. Port utilization down ~60%. We'll keep it up for 2h and evaluate.
Alex W: follow-ups: (a) make autoscaler less bursty for GPU pools by default, (b) add egress capacity playbook for eu-west, (c) evaluate moving attach/storage calls to private peering to avoid NAT.
Maria S: I'll write the playbook and a PR for CA defaults.
Ryan (oncall): leaving a note in oncall log and runbook: incident label "snat-bleed->controller-elector-flap".
Jin (infra): will run cost/benefit for permanent NAT scale vs peering. Initial guess: peering cheaper long-run but requires infra work.
Alex W: great work team, keep me posted in this thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
Maria S: will post postmortem if we need one.
Ryan (oncall): rolling to standby, sounds stable for now.
